question: What is the minimum length of a rental contract for a primary residence if the landlord is an individual?
reference_answer: Five years: if a shorter term is agreed, the contract is renewed compulsorily year by year up to five years, unless the tenant gives at least 30 days' notice that they do not want to renew.

question: When can a tenant leave before the end of a primary-residence lease and how much notice must they give?
reference_answer: After at least six months, giving the landlord at least thirty days' notice; it gives the landlord no right to compensation.

question: How much cash deposit (fianza) has to be paid when signing a residential lease?
reference_answer: One month's rent (two months for leases for uses other than housing).

question: On which days of the month must rent be paid if the contract says nothing?
reference_answer: Unless agreed otherwise, rent is paid monthly within the first seven days of the month; the landlord cannot demand more than one month in advance.

question: My contract says nothing about updating the rent. Can the landlord raise it every year?
reference_answer: No. Without an express agreement the rent is not updated.

question: If the tenant dies, within what period must the landlord be notified so that a family member can take over the lease?
reference_answer: Three months from the death, in writing, with the registered death certificate and the identity of the person taking over; otherwise the lease ends.

question: My landlord is doing maintenance works in my flat that will last a month. Do I have to put up with them, and do I get a rent reduction?
reference_answer: If the works cannot wait until the lease ends the tenant must accept them; if they last more than twenty days the rent is reduced in proportion to the part of the home the tenant cannot use.

question: How much notice must the landlord give before doing improvement works in the rented home?
reference_answer: In writing, at least three months in advance, stating the nature, start, duration and expected cost; the tenant may withdraw from the contract within one month.

question: Can I sublet the whole flat I am renting?
reference_answer: No. It can only be sublet partially and with the landlord's written consent; the sublet rent cannot exceed the rent of the lease.

question: How long can a temporary housing lease last?
reference_answer: More than thirty-one days and, as a general rule, no more than twelve months in total, depending on the reason for the temporary stay.

question: In a temporary housing lease, when can the tenant withdraw and with how much notice?
reference_answer: Once at least one month has passed since signing, giving at least ten days' notice.

question: Can I knock down a partition wall in my rented flat without the landlord's permission?
reference_answer: No. Works that change the layout of the home need the landlord's written consent; otherwise the landlord can demand that it be restored or terminate the contract.

question: My landlord has not returned my deposit after the lease ended. Does it earn interest?
reference_answer: Yes. The balance to be returned earns the statutory interest rate once one month has passed since the keys were handed back without it being returned.

question: Can the landlord require me to take out rent-default insurance?
reference_answer: No. The tenant can never be required to take out rent-default insurance or similar cover.

question: Can the landlord take the home back before five years to live in it himself?
reference_answer: Only if the landlord is an individual, the first year has passed and that need was stated expressly in the contract; they must give at least two months' notice.

question: What criteria are used to declare a stressed residential market area (zona de mercado residencial tensionado)?
reference_answer: That the average cost of mortgage or rent plus expenses and basic utilities exceeds 30% of average household income, or that prices have grown in the previous five years at least three percentage points more than the regional CPI.

question: Can I ask whether the flat contains asbestos before signing the lease?
reference_answer: Yes. A prospective tenant can request information on the presence of asbestos or other hazardous substances before the contract is signed.

question: What is the minimum size of an owners' association's reserve fund?
reference_answer: It cannot be less than 10% of its latest ordinary budget.

question: What court procedure can the owners' association use to claim unpaid fees from a neighbour?
reference_answer: The special payment-order procedure (proceso monitorio) for owners' associations, attaching a certificate of the agreement settling the debt (other procedures remain available).

question: A neighbour carries out disturbing activities in his flat. Who must demand that he stop?
reference_answer: The president of the owners' association, on their own initiative or at the request of any owner or occupant, demands that the activity stop immediately, warning of legal action.

question: If I rent a flat out by rooms, is there a limit on the total rent?
reference_answer: Yes. The sum of the rents of the room contracts in force at the same time cannot exceed the rent for the whole home.

question: Can I sign a clause in the contract waiving my right of first refusal (tanteo y retracto)?
reference_answer: No. The parties cannot agree that the tenant waives the preferential right to buy.

question: I am renting to a company (a legal entity) for three years. What is the minimum length of the contract and how much notice must the landlord give if they do not want to renew it at the end?
reference_answer: Seven years minimum because the landlord is a legal entity; at expiry the landlord must give at least four months' notice (the tenant two), otherwise it renews annually for up to three more years.

question: What is a large landlord (gran tenedor) and what must they do if a vulnerable tenant asks for the extraordinary extension at the end of the contract?
reference_answer: Someone who owns more than ten residential urban properties or more than 1,500 m² of residential floor space (excluding garages and storage rooms); they must accept the extraordinary extension of up to one year if the tenant proves vulnerability with a social-services report.

question: On a five-year residential lease, can the landlord charge me the estate agency fees, and how much can they ask as a guarantee on top of the deposit?
reference_answer: No: property management and contract formalisation costs cannot be passed on to the tenant. The additional guarantee cannot exceed two months' rent.

question: I want to rent my flat to tourists. Is that governed by the LAU, and what majority does the owners' association need to limit or ban it?
reference_answer: No: tourist lets under a specific regime are excluded from the LAU. An agreement approving, limiting or banning them needs three fifths of the owners representing three fifths of the ownership shares.

question: How long does a stressed-area declaration last, and how much can the rent of a new contract in that area rise compared with the previous one?
reference_answer: Three years, extendable annually. The initial rent cannot exceed that of the last contract in force in the previous five years (as updated), except for an extra 10% in cases such as renovation, energy improvement, accessibility or contracts of ten years or more.

question: My landlord is selling the flat. Do I have a right to buy it first and within what period, and must the buyer respect my lease?
reference_answer: Yes, a right of first refusal within 30 calendar days of formal notice (right of redemption if not notified). The buyer takes over the lease for the first five years (seven if the landlord was a legal entity).

question: My landlord will not carry out necessary repairs. Can I terminate the contract, and how long do they have to reply if I send them a written quote?
reference_answer: Yes, failure to carry out the repairs in Article 21 allows the tenant to terminate the contract. After a written request with a quote the landlord has fifteen calendar days; if they do not reply the tenant may do the work and deduct it from the rent.

question: Within what period must the occupant of a home produce a title justifying their possession when the owner asks a court for immediate recovery of a squatted home?
reference_answer: The corpus (LAU, Housing Law, LPH) does not regulate the procedure for recovering illegally occupied homes; the assistant should say it does not cover this.

question: What is the value of the IRAV rent index that the INE has published this month?
reference_answer: The corpus defines the IRAV as the cap on rent updates but does not contain its published value; it should say it does not know and point to the INE.

question: Which municipalities in Catalonia have been declared stressed residential market areas?
reference_answer: The corpus regulates how stressed areas are declared but does not list the declared areas; it should say it does not cover this.

question: How much Property Transfer Tax (ITP) does the tenant pay when signing a lease?
reference_answer: The corpus does not regulate ITP; it should say it does not cover this.

question: How much money per month does the Bono Alquiler Joven (youth rent subsidy) pay and who can apply?
reference_answer: The corpus does not regulate the Bono Alquiler Joven; it should say it does not cover this.

question: What prison sentence does the crime of squatting in a home (usurpación) carry?
reference_answer: The corpus does not contain the Criminal Code; it should say it does not cover this.

question: Within what period must the deposit be lodged with the Community of Madrid's agency, and what is the fine if it is not?
reference_answer: The LAU lets regions require deposits to be lodged but the corpus does not contain Madrid's rules; it should say it does not cover the period or the fine.
